newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine millers seek speedier corn imports.
newsitem.headline: Philippine millers seek speedier corn imports.

text.p: Philippine livestock farmers and feed millers have asked the National Food Authority to speed up the importation of corn due to rising demand, government and industry officials said on Tuesday.

"The National Federation of Hog Raisers has asked the Department of Agriculture to order the NFA to import an additional 300,000 tonnes on top of the 117,000 tonnes of yellow maize bought by the government for the private sector," a senior Agriculture Department official who requested not to be named told Reuters.
But other livestock raisers and feed millers have asked higher volumes, or at least an additional 424,000 tonnes, an industry official said.

All corn imports done by the NFA are slapped a lower 35 percent when these are included in the country's minimum access volume, or the minimum level of grain imports the country has to import in compliance with its commitment to World Trade Organisation rules.
Last week, Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero told reporters the department has approved the application of a private company to import 25,000 tonnes of white corn for starch from South Africa.
Philippine government officials said South Africa is seriously courting the Philippines to be able to sell corn.
In a previous interview, Escudero said demand for white corn from Philippine food manufacturers is rising.
The Philippines has been importing largely yellow corn for animal feed.
The NFA is expected to take delivery of an initial batch 30,000 tonnes of yellow maize from China on March 10 and 11. Three others ships carrying a total of 77,000 tonnes for the rest of the month.
